A drawing can support several calculations. The physical problem determines
what is excited, which boundaries are imposed and what the answer means.

## Capacitance: charge response to conductor voltage

Electrostatic extraction solves for conductor charge under specified terminal
voltages. A capacitance matrix relates charge and voltage, with conductor order
and ground choices carried by the model. It can supply a circuit's pad-to-ground
or mutual capacitance. Palace Electrostatic and Q3D are the implemented paths.
A finite enclosure grounded at its exterior is a different model from one with
only selected physical conductors grounded.

## Resonance: modes of a field and circuit model

An Eigenmode calculation finds the resonant frequencies and fields of the
specified model. A linearized junction can be represented by an inductive
branch. That branch participates in the mode; it is not supplied by the drawn
pad alone. For an ideal lumped LC model, $f_0=1/(2\pi\sqrt{LC})$ gives a useful
interpretive reference, while the electromagnetic model includes distributed
fields and its chosen boundaries.

Palace and HFSS provide the implemented Eigenmode paths. Optional EPR analysis
asks where the mode stores energy and what selected loss assumptions imply.
Read [energy participation](../eigenmode-epr.qmd) before interpreting those fractions.

## Driven response: excite a port at a frequency

A driven problem asks how the model responds to an applied excitation.
HFSS Modal and Terminal workflows expose complex S-parameters. The port model,
reference conductor or integration direction is part of the problem. A peak in
a driven response is not the same data structure as an Eigenmode result.

## Finite extraction versus a cross section

Q3D extracts conductor matrices for a finite three-dimensional model. Q2D
extracts per-unit-length properties of an explicitly authored cross section.
Neither automatically replaces the other. A finite length, end geometry and
port treatment cannot be recovered from a per-length matrix alone.

::: {.callout-tip title="Choose a quantity before a solver"}
Write down the conductor pair, mode or port response you need, its units and
the intended circuit-model use. Then choose a supported workflow from the
[capability table](../backend-support.qmd).
:::

For native formulations, see [Palace problem types](https://awslabs.github.io/palace/stable/guide/problem/)
and the [PyAEDT user guide](https://aedt.docs.pyansys.com/version/stable/User_guide/index.html).
